title: Track restart-required per output component instead of only globally
why: UiStatus's docstring already reserves a restart_required value, but only a single global _restart_required flag exists today (mediainfo/configui/output.py), flipped by any outputs.* edit - a user editing one output has no way to tell which specific display actually needs restarting.
what: Extend restart tracking from ConfigStore.save_form's single global flag to record which specific outputs.* config paths changed since the last restart, then thread that through to UiComponent.status.
notes:
2026-07-23 dispatched to background agent `a129971bd99527f17`
2026-07-25 Implemented per-output-type restart tracking, additive to the existing global _restart_required flag. ConfigStore.save_form/save_raw/restore_backup now return a third value, changed_output_types: FrozenSet[str] - save_form returns exactly the OUTPUT_CONFIG_TYPES keys actually merged from the posted outputs dict (matches the client's existing one-output-type-per-save flow); save_raw/restore_backup conservatively return every registered output type (they can rewrite the whole file with no per-field provenance), mirroring their existing 'assume a restart might be needed' reasoning for the global flag. ConfigUiOutput accumulates these into a new in-memory self._restart_required_outputs: Set[str], cleared by /api/restart alongside _restart_required. Threaded into ui_builder.build_components()/_output_components(), which now sets each output UiComponent.requires_restart from membership in that set (was hardcoded True for every output) and status to the (now-implemented) 'restart_required' value via _status_for's new parameter, ranked below disabled/needs_configuration but above health-derived status. UiModel's UiStatus comment updated to drop the stale 'not derivable per component' note. Global UiDashboard.restart_required and the Restart button are unchanged (save_form's blanket bool computation kept, just decomposed by type). One deliberate edge-case narrowing, not exercised by any test: previously bool(outputs) counted an all-unknown-output-type payload toward restart_required; now only recognized+merged types count. Truth-grounding: background/context in the prompt matched the code as found exactly, no discrepancies. Verification: ruff check --fix mediainfo (clean), ruff format mediainfo (145 files unchanged), mypy mediainfo (Success: no issues found in 145 source files), pytest tests/test_config_ui.py tests/test_ui_model.py (215 passed). Test coverage for this mechanism is explicitly deferred to roadmap task 004 per the task's own chain description, not added here. Decision doc: docs/foreman/001.md.

why: H5 unified the config UI nav specifically to fix users losing their mental map, but History and Help (both added since) brought the sidebar back up to 11 top-level items, re-fragmenting the exact thing H5 fixed.
what: Nest Pipeline as a tab/section inside Dashboard (client-side routing only, dashboard.js renderSection()) and History as a tab inside Library, dropping two entries from NAV_SECTIONS/dashboard.html without removing either feature. Also reconsider whether Help needs a full nav slot versus a footer icon next to Theme/Hitster-safe.
notes:

title: Sort or badge commonly-used plugins ahead of niche ones on Media/Metadata/Displays pages
why: 18 sources / 19 enrichers / 15 outputs all render as one unsorted, unbadged list, so a fresh install looks equally complex to a Kodi-only household and a Kodi+Sonos+HA+Plex one.
what: Add a lightweight commonly-used/popular marker (or a configured-first default sort) to the card grid in components.js so a new install's Media/Metadata/Displays pages surface likely-relevant plugins first instead of one flat alphabetical list of 15-19 cards.
notes: 2026-07-26 Added a static common:bool field to UiComponent (ui_model.py), set in ui_builder.py from curated per-family frozensets (_COMMON_SOURCE_TYPES: kodi/plex/spotify/sonos/homeassistant/jellyfin; _COMMON_ENRICHER_TYPES: musicbrainz/fanarttv/tmdb/thetvdb/wikipedia/lrclib; _COMMON_OUTPUT_TYPES: web/pixoo/mqtt/folder). components.js sortCardsByRelevance() ranks enabled first, then common, then alphabetical, applied in renderCategorySection(). A small outlined Popular badge (componentCard()) shows only when common && !enabled, avoiding redundancy with the status badge. Verified visually with an isolated instance + Playwright: Media page shows the 6 curated sources first with Popular badges; Displays page shows Web/Folder (enabled+common) with no redundant badge while Pixoo/MQTT (disabled+common) show Popular. Verification: ruff/mypy clean on Python, node --check clean on JS, full pytest tests/test_config_ui.py tests/test_ui_model.py tests/test_dashboard_shell.py (245 passed). Decision doc: docs/foreman/006.md.

title: YouTube source has no artwork fallback for non-music videos
why: youtube.py forces media_type=music and relies on music enrichers keyed off channel-as-artist; non-music videos get 0 images, so folder/pixoo_16 outputs fall back to idle wallpapers instead of showing anything for the actual now-playing item
what: Investigate mediainfo/sources/youtube.py and give non-music YouTube videos a usable artwork fallback (e.g. YouTube thumbnail) when music-enricher lookup finds nothing, without breaking existing music-video artwork matching.
notes: 2026-08-01 Scope expanded by user: agent found ADB dumpsys media_session exposes no video ID/thumbnail, only title/channel text. User approved adding YouTube Data API v3 lookup (search by title+channel -> video ID -> thumbnail URL), config-gated with an API key like other enrichers (e.g. fanart.tv), disabled by default, graceful degradation if key missing or lookup fails/no match.

title: Add test coverage for multi-instance output test-connection button
why: runDetailTest() in mediainfo/outputs/static/config_ui/components.js:930 had a bug where it always built the /api/test/output request body from detailOutputsWorking[0] instead of detailOutputsWorking[detailInstanceIndex], so clicking Test connection on a second instance of a multi-instance output (e.g. a 2nd Pixoo) always tested the first instance instead. Fixed in commit 840119f, but no existing test would have caught it - tests/test_config_ui.py and tests/test_config_ui_playwright_smoke.py have no coverage of the instance picker (detailInstanceIndex) combined with the test-connection action.
what: Add a Playwright smoke test (or extend test_config_ui_playwright_smoke.py) that: adds a 2nd instance to a multi-instance output (e.g. pixoo), selects it via the instance picker, clicks Test connection, and asserts the outgoing /api/test/output request body reflects the 2nd instance's fields (not the 1st).

title: Add test coverage for cache._atomic_save and web output image-retry behavior
why: Commit 9ed6fb2 added mediainfo/cache.py:_atomic_save (atomic write for get_transformed_path/get_derived_path) and a retry-on-error loop in mediainfo/outputs/templates/web/index.html showImage(), but neither has direct test coverage - existing tests only verify end-to-end cache/web behavior, not the atomicity or retry/backoff logic itself.
what: Add a test that exercises _atomic_save writing to a temp file (dir=out_path.parent) then os.replace, including the cleanup-on-exception path (tmp_path.unlink on BaseException). For the frontend retry logic (showImage/load() in index.html), add a browser-level or scripted test (e.g. via a headless browser harness if one exists in this repo, per reference_headless_browser memory) verifying: (1) onerror triggers a retry with a cache-busting query param, (2) MAX_IMAGE_RETRIES=5 is respected and it gives up after exhausting retries while keeping the last-visible image, (3) the showToken generation counter correctly discards a stale retry when a newer image supersedes it mid-retry.

title: Make get_derived_path json sidecar write atomic
why: mediainfo/cache.py:get_derived_path writes the PNG via _atomic_save (added in commit 9ed6fb2) but still writes its metadata sidecar with (base_dir / f"{key}.json").write_text(...) directly to the final path, non-atomically - same partial-write class of bug as the image writes just fixed, just for the json sidecar (used by Pixoo text-removal decision records).
what: In mediainfo/cache.py get_derived_path, replace the direct (base_dir / f"{key}.json").write_text(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2), encoding="utf-8") with a write-to-temp-then-os.replace pattern in the same directory, mirroring _atomic_save (or extend _atomic_save/add a small sibling helper for text content).
notes: 2026-08-10 2026-08-10 Added _atomic_write_text (mirrors _atomic_save: mkstemp in the same dir, write, os.replace, unlink-on-exception) and used it for the JSON sidecar write in get_derived_path. Existing tests in tests/test_cache.py (e.g. test_get_derived_path_writes_metadata_sidecar_when_build_returns_a_tuple) already covered the sidecar content/behavior and pass unchanged.
